about_title: About the African Labour Research and Education Institute
about_subtitle: ALREI is the research and education institute of ITUC-Africa. It strengthens the African trade union movement through labor research, workers' education, evidence-based advocacy, and collaboration.
our_history_text_1: The African Labour Research and Education Institute (ALREI) is a semi-autonomous institute of the African Regional Organisation of the International Trade Union Confederation (ITUC-Africa). It was established to meet the research and education needs of African trade unions and to strengthen their capacity to represent workers and influence policy.
our_history_text_2: A feasibility study conducted in 2014 highlighted gaps across the continent. Many trade unions needed stronger mechanisms to conduct research and use evidence. ITUC-Africa therefore established ALREI to make structured training and knowledge accessible to trade unionists across countries, sectors, and languages.
vision_desc: To be an African center of excellence on the world of work and workers' rights.
mission_desc: Equip trade unions with practical knowledge and tools for effective action.
pedagogy_subtitle: ALREI workers' education rests on 6 core principles focused on empowering workers.
governance_text: ALREI operates under the strategic supervision of an Advisory Board and the ITUC-Africa General Council. The Advisory Board reviews policies, plans, budgets, and compliance with ethical rules.

course_1_title: TULDA 2026: Digital Trade, Tax Justice and Decent Work in Africa
course_1_desc: The sixth Trade Union Leadership Development Academy focuses on digital trade, tax justice, and decent work in Africa. It helps young trade unionists understand digital transformations and build concrete trade union responses.
course_1_format: Hybrid training (Online phase + Residential phase in Lomé)
course_1_schedule: Online phase: Oct 29-30, 2026 | Residential phase: Nov 2026 in Lomé, Togo
course_2_title: Training Manual for Organizing Campaigns in the Informal Economy
course_2_desc: An online training course and practical toolkit for planning organizing campaigns, mobilizing informal economy workers, identifying leaders, and strengthening workers' power.
course_3_desc: A worker-centered training program dedicated to the effects of climate change, just transition demands, worker participation, and trade union strategies for equitable transitions.
course_3_format: Online and hybrid training (French, English, Kiswahili)
blog_1_title: Upcoming Opening of Applications for TULDA 2026
blog_1_desc: The sixth Trade Union Leadership Development Academy will combine online training and a residential phase in Lomé to help young African trade unionists address digital trade, taxation, and labor market transformations.
blog_2_title: New Online Training on Organizing in the Informal Economy
blog_2_desc: A new Africa-focused online training resource will help union organizers and educators plan campaigns, recruit and mobilize workers, develop leaders, and build workers' power.
blog_3_title: Training Program on Climate Change and Just Transition Available Online in 2026
blog_3_desc: A new online and hybrid program will help African trade unions understand climate change impacts, define their just transition demands, and strengthen workers' power.
pricing_free_desc: Introductory guides, videos, and thematic fact sheets accessible to all trade unionists with no registration fees.
pricing_cohort_desc: Hybrid certifying training (online and residential) with participation scholarships awarded following application selection.
pricing_custom_card_desc: Custom programs organized specifically for a national trade union center, federation, or partner institution.
faq_q1: How do I enroll in an ALREI training program?
faq_a1: To enroll, create an account or sign in, then browse the course catalog. Click on your desired program and follow the enrollment instructions.
faq_a2: Yes, every participant who successfully completes program requirements receives an official certificate of completion issued by the ALREI Institute and ITUC-Africa.
faq_q3: Who can participate in ALREI programs?
faq_a3: Programs are open to trade unionists, labor educators, researchers, and labor movement actors across Africa. Some programs are open access, while others require application or union nomination.
privacy_sec1_desc: ALREI collects only the information necessary to manage your account, enroll you in training programs, and issue certificates (full name, email, trade union organization, country).
privacy_sec2_desc: Your data is used exclusively to grant training access, inform you of new programs, and evaluate the impact of ALREI and ITUC-Africa training activities.
privacy_sec3_desc: In accordance with data protection regulations, you may request access, correction, or deletion of your personal data at any time by contacting the ALREI team at alrei{'@'}ituc-africa.org.
